A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoSTE and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The shared material can be matched reliably, including relocated displays; v3 adds Appendix G.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices E–F report original fine-tuning evaluations on Pythia, Qwen, and Llama, together with rotation ablations and activation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, KV-cache precision comparisons, and training-cost measurements in Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same rotation selection, quantization-error objective, and STE updates. The implemented K = 1 configuration also remains unchanged. Explicitly explaining the identity-versus-Hadamard choice clarifies an existing component.

E1.justification: Both versions use Reddit TL;DR summarization and Tulu 3 fine-tuning with the same six downstream benchmarks. The represented tasks, datasets, and model families remain unchanged; additional quantization configurations do not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 7–8 add QLoRA comparisons across four Pythia/Qwen models and DuQuant comparisons for both Qwen models, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives, particularly low-rank fine-tuning. Table 10 also compares LoRA training costs. LLM-QAT is removed from main Table 1, but its identical Pythia comparison remains in Table 7.

E3.justification: v3 adds W4A4KV8 settings for QuaRot and DuQuant, rank-64 low-rank comparisons, and peak GPU memory as an evaluation measure. The existing calibration, training, and downstream evaluation settings in Appendices C–D and Tables 4–6 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 8 adds KV-cache precision sensitivity comparisons, holding weights and activations at four bits while comparing four- and eight-bit caches. Appendix G adds computational-cost analysis. The existing rotation ablation and outlier analyses in Table 3 and Figures 3–4 and 6–7 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new training-cost statistics are point measurements, and the description of significant DuQuant degradation does not introduce statistical testing.

E6.justification: v3 adds baseline, KV8, and Qwen training-cost results while retaining all existing RoSTE accuracy scores. Newly evaluated QLoRA scores 23.32 against RoSTE's unchanged 25.10 on Qwen2.5-7B W4A4KV4, explaining the new 1.78-point comparison in Section 5.1. Table 8 also changes QuaRot's Qwen2.5-7B W4A8KV4 average from 4.00 to 3.99.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, Theorem 4.3, Proposition 4.4, and proofs in Appendices A–B remain unchanged. The explanatory feature notation following Assumption 4.2 is corrected to the quantized-rotated features already specified by that assumption; no new mathematical argument is introduced.

C1.justification: The conclusion refocuses novelty on combining adaptive rotation with the fine-tuning objective. Section 3 removes the claim of the first direct STE application to SFT. The abstract and principal methodological, theoretical, and performance contributions remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: The introduction replaces a definite claim that existing PTQ rotations permit outliers to re-emerge with uncertainty about applying PTQ before or after fine-tuning. Section 5 qualifies expected benefits from larger K by mentioning larger datasets. Appendix G newly interprets RoSTE's computational costs as similar to those of comparators.

D1.justification: v3 specifies rank 64 for the new low-rank comparisons and reports training time and peak memory in Table 10. The advertised code location changes from Hong-Lab-UMN-ECE/RoSTE to OptimAI-Lab/RoSTE. Existing implementation instructions and training hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the DuQuant citation and discusses its comparison results. QLoRA and LLM-QAT were already cited in v2. Removing the first-direct-STE novelty claim and refocusing the conclusion modestly refine the positioning relative to earlier work.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording edits and expands explanations of the optimization formulation, algorithm, theory, and Qwen results. It adds acknowledgements and Appendix G while retaining the existing main section order and overall narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 1 to page 2 and changes from two stacked panels to three horizontal panels, adding Qwen. Table 1 is enlarged, Table 2 and Figure 3 move, Tables 7–8 gain rows, and Table 10 is added. The other existing figure contents are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added QLoRA/DuQuant comparisons, KV-cache sensitivity evidence, and training-cost table make the empirical assessment more informative while preserving the original method, proofs, and accuracy results. The benefit is limited by Appendix G's overly broad similar-cost interpretation: Table 10 reports RoSTE at 2.8 hours and 318 GB versus QLoRA at 0.83 hours and 98 GB. Nevertheless, exposing this tradeoff improves transparency overall.
